# Lighting and Material Interaction

Also called: Per-Splat Relighting, Photon Splatting, Splat Painting

## Overview
This family defines how photometric properties and illumination are computed for splatted primitives, addressing the gap between raw geometric density and visually plausible appearance. It differs from sibling methods like [EWA Splatting](1069-ewa-splatting.md) or [Ray-Driven Splatting](1156-ray-driven-splatting.md) by explicitly decoupling the [shading model](#837-shading-models.md) from the rasterization footprint, allowing for dynamic lighting, baked global illumination, or direct user editing of material properties per primitive [S1, 3371-per-splat-relighting.md].

## Shared principles
The [splatting](#23-splatting.md) family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].

1.  **Primitive Representation:** The volume is decomposed into primitives. These may be explicit geometric shapes (cubes, cells, splats) or implicit functions sampled via texture hardware [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. Each primitive $k$ is defined by its position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $g_k$ or $\rho_k$, and a reconstruction kernel $h$ (typically a Gaussian) [S1][S6][S10, unofficial].
2.  **Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., [shear-warp](#24-shear-warp.md)) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., [EWA splatting](#1069-ewa-splatting.md)) to account for foreshortening [S6][S10, unofficial].
3.  **Rasterization:** The transformed primitives are projected onto the 2D image plane. This step leverages hardware-accelerated scan-conversion, depth testing, and blending [S1, S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. The contribution of a voxel $D$ to a screen point $(x,y)$ is determined by the [footprint function](#4731-footprint-function-mechanism.md) $F(x,y)$, which is the integral of the 3D kernel along the view direction [S2, unofficial][S6][S10, unofficial]:
    $$ F(x,y) = \int h(x-x_D, y-y_D, z) \, dz $$
    The intensity written to the pixel is modulated by the voxel density:
    $$ P(x,y) = \text{weight}(x,y) \cdot \rho(D) $$
    where $\text{weight}(x,y) = F(x-x_D, y-y_D)$ [S10, unofficial].
4.  **[Compositing](#2436-compositing.md):** Contributions are accumulated to form the final image. This is typically done using [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) in back-to-front or front-to-back order to handle transparency correctly [S1, S2, S3, unofficial][S7, book]. Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, unofficial].
5.  **Hardware [Acceleration](#18-acceleration.md):** Most methods in this family rely on GPU rasterization pipelines for performance, enabling real-time interactivity [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Photon Splatting](2832-photon-splatting.md)
[Photon Splatting](#2832-photon-splatting.md) captures direct illumination by rasterizing a light-view map and projecting photons into a sparse voxel [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) [2832-photon-splatting.md]. It solves the problem of efficiently storing incoming radiance as a direction distribution and energy proportional to the subtended solid angle of the light source [2832-photon-splatting.md]. It differs from [Per-Splat Relighting](3371-per-splat-relighting.md) by [baking lighting](#2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md) information directly into the voxel data structure during a [pre-computation](#2330-pre-computation.md) phase, rather than computing shading dynamically per splat during rendering [2832-photon-splatting.md, 3371-per-splat-relighting.md].

### [Per-Splat Relighting](3371-per-splat-relighting.md)
[Per-Splat Relighting](#3371-per-splat-relighting.md) computes a dynamic lighting multiplier for each Gaussian splat based on its world position, normal, ambient occlusion, and confidence, enabling real-time dynamic illumination [3371-per-splat-relighting.md]. It differs from pre-shading by deferring photometric calculations to the rendering pass, allowing interactive light changes while avoiding the complexity of full path tracing by treating each splat as an independent shading unit [3371-per-splat-relighting.md].

### Splat Painting
**Definition:** Recolorization or shadow additions by checking if a splat center intersects with a spherical brush and adjusting its color value [S1].
**Parameters:** Color channels are stored in 16-bit format to support brushes with smooth falloff and low opacity [S1].
**Pitfalls:** Splat models often do not lend themselves well to painting detailed features (text, lines, symbols) because they represent sparse geometry; models from images use few splats on clean surfaces, preventing detailed color changes [S1]. Color leaks may occur into differently colored parts of a surface if state-of-the-art Gaussian splat reconstructions rarely feature clean and opaque surfaces [S1].

## Background
The techniques described herein originate from the practical requirements of editing and rendering large-scale Gaussian Splat models, specifically detailed in the development of "Splatshop" [S1]. While standard splatting focuses on geometric reconstruction and rasterization efficiency, these methods address the need for dynamic lighting, global illumination approximation, and artistic control over the resulting visual appearance.

## Sources
